name: Matte top coat nails

card.summary: A clear top coat that dries to a flat, non-shiny finish, giving nails a polished, understated look.
card.note: Polish ingredients vary by brand; some people react to certain formulas.

quick.overview:
A matte top coat is a clear polish applied over bare nails or colored polish that dries without shine. It gives nails an even, soft, flat finish instead of a glossy one.

Some men use it as a low-key way to neaten nails, since a matte clear coat reads as groomed without looking painted.
quick.how: It goes on as the last layer, over a base coat or color, and wears off with time or is removed with polish remover. It is usually used as part of routine nail care.
quick.risks: Polish risks are modest and ingredient dependent; the health effects of some ingredients are disputed, and the US HHS regards occasional consumer risk as low. Some gel formulas have caused skin or respiratory reactions.

lead: A top coat is a clear final layer of nail polish that hardens into a protective barrier and adds finish; a matte version gives a flat finish in place of shine.[1]
People use it to make nails look tidy and uniform. Polish has long been worn for appearance, and men wearing clear or colored polish do so for protection, a polished look or self-expression.[1]

angle.text: A matte top coat evens the look of the nail surface without gloss, for a subtle groomed finish.

paras: Nail polish categories include base coats, color, top coats (a hardened clear barrier against chips and scratches) and gel polish cured under UV or LED light.[1] Matte top coats are a finish variant of the top coat.

Health risks of polish ingredients such as phthalates and the so-called "toxic trio" are disputed; several manufacturers phased out dibutyl phthalate in 2006 and HHS considers occasional consumer risk low.[1] Gel products containing MMA and HEMA have caused skin and respiratory reactions and are restricted in some places.[1]
